Line-break handling is generic, never a 117 per-source choice. 118 - **A supported/registered host is necessary but not sufficient for "an 119 event"** — gating on `Boolean(site)` surfaced phantom events on home pages 120 (#133); a real event requires actual data (JSON-LD or a parsed date), never a 121 mere host match. 122 123 ## Workflow-failure classification 124 125 **Mind the one gap `gha/scheduled-failure-escalation` can't see:** it only 126 inspects workflows carrying a `schedule:`, so a workflow that is unattended by 127 some *other* trigger — `workflow_run`, `repository_dispatch` — needs its failure 128 job wired by hand. 129 The `Release` stub (`chrome-extension-release.yml`) is exactly that shape; its 130 reporters live in the vendored create-package/publish/daily workflows it calls. 131 132 ## Extractor pipeline 133 134 Standing rules for the extractor-automation domain — the two gcec pack 135 [`tasks/`](tasks/): **create-extractor** (an `extractor-request` issue → a PR 136 adding site support, and the sweep that records a committed `.url`'s missing 137 cached page) and the weekly **generic-extractor-improvements** (read a spec only when working 138 on that pipeline). Adding or refreshing a cached live case by hand is the 139 [testing-guide](skills/testing-guide/SKILL.md) skill. 140 141 - **All page fetching goes through [`scraperapi.mjs`](tasks/create-extractor/scraperapi.mjs), from a 142 task's preprocessing worker and nowhere else.** A rendered fetch through 143 ScraperAPI's residential proxy (`render=true`, so a single-page app records 144 post-render HTML with real data). Bot-blocking from CI/sandbox IPs is the 145 portable rule maintained in the canon; here the escape hatch is the 146 `SCRAPER_API_KEY` **GitHub Actions secret**, named in both tasks' 147 `required_secrets` — never a local fetch (this sandbox is bot-blocked), and 148 never an agent session. ScraperAPI is the whole fetching surface — swap the 149 vendor in that one module if it underperforms. The aid for a flaky SPA render is 150 the **`Wait-for selector`** a source request can carry 151 (`extension/events-popup/derive-wait-selector.js`, a source-request tool, NOT an 152 event extractor, #603), passed through as `wait_for_selector`. 153 - **Facebook can't be a cached live case** — a hard HTTP 400 even through the 154 proxy, so its extraction stays unit-tests-only 155 (`extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`). 156 - **Rendered output isn't deterministic.** A re-record can legitimately shift a 157 live case's `expected` — treat such drift like a site-markup change, and prefer 158 extracting JSON-LD/`og:` (which apps still inject) over brittle DOM positions. 159 - **An ambiguous numeric slash date is read by the page's declared locale, 160 centrally — never per-source, never guessed.** `"05/07/2026"` (both parts ≤ 12) 161 reads month-first by default (V8's US convention) and flips day-first only on a 162 *positive* non-US signal — an explicit non-US region in `` / 163 `og:locale`, or a non-English language; a bare `en` (region unknown) stays 164 month-first rather than guess. Resolution lives in `helpers/dates.js` 165 (`parseDateFromText` / `normalizeDateValue` take a `dayFirst` flag, threaded 166 from `generic-extractor.js`'s `pageUsesDayFirstDates`), mirroring 167 `derive-timezone.js`'s locale read; unambiguous dates (a part > 12) and the 168 `.` / `-` separators are always day-first regardless (#686). 169 - **An unrecordable page is a dead end, not a failed run.** When a fetch can't 170 produce a page (bot wall, dead URL, empty render), create-extractor's 171 preprocessing labels the request `needs-human` with the reason 172 and exits **0** — a task failure would converge to a `needs-human` dispatch 173 issue as well, duplicating the signal and implying the pipeline broke when it 174 correctly declined. Same for the pending-page sweep: the pages that did record still land. 175 - **The generic-coverage gate is a high-watermark over a changing case set.** A 176 removed/renamed case the watermark still lists makes it stale: the local refresh re-anchors it 177 (commit that); in CI it's an error to fix. *Caveat:* never commit a re-anchored 178 baseline while the gate is red — a regression bundled with a case-set change can 179 be re-anchored over. Detailed mechanics self-document in the gate's own headers 180 (`dev/requirements/extractor/generic-coverage/generic-coverage.js` / `.test.js`). 181 - **To see what the core generic extractor gets ON ITS OWN** on any cached page — 182 even a supported host — load the files, set `GCal.sources = []`, then call 183 `GCal.extract()`: the documented way to strip every per-site override and see 184 the bare base through the same norm/sort the popup uses. (`GCal.extract()` 185 alone no longer answers this: the generic extractor is the base layer of every 186 extraction now, so on a supported host its output already carries the site's 187 overrides.) Most start/end *differences* vs a dedicated source are just its 188 hardcoded `ctz` localizing to floating time (same instant), not extraction 189 bugs; the real gaps are fields it can't know generically (durations, 190 site-specific descriptions, and — where the page doesn't declare corroborating 191 hints, see `helpers/derive-timezone.js` — `ctz`). This is the comparison the 192 generic-coverage gate automates — and a case where it shows NO gap is a 193 candidate for deleting the per-site source and listing the host in 194 `supportedDomains`). 195 196 ## Architecture rules of the road 197 198 Whenever we agree on a new or changed top-level architectural guideline, update 199 this section as part of the same change (the design doc itself is 200 `dev/procedures/highLevelDesign.md`): 201 202 - **`extension/event-extractors/custom/` is the extensibility point — one file 203 per site, and nothing else.** The rest of `event-extractors/` is the pipeline 204 itself: the registry, the orchestrator, the shared helpers, and the one core 205 generic extractor (`generic-extractor.js`), which is a different kind of thing 206 from a per-site file. 207 - **The core generic extractor is the base layer of every extraction** — it runs 208 on every page, and a per-site source is only a layer of *overrides* merged over 209 it, stating the fields it gets better. A source never re-reads what the page 210 already says about itself, and the generic extractor may never know about a 211 specific site. 212 - **Being supported is DECLARED, never derived from the extractors.** 213 `supportedDomains` in `extension/host-lists.json` is the one list of hosts 214 we claim, read directly by the toolbar worker and the popup. Never add a second 215 list, and never register a placeholder source just to make a host count as 216 supported. The only guarded direction is that every per-site source's host 217 appears in the list. 218 - **A site we fully support gets no extractor file when there is nothing to 219 override.** It stays listed in `supportedDomains` and stays fully supported — 220 green icon, no correction prompt — with no file at all. When a 221 `custom/.js` shrinks to nothing, just delete it; when such a site starts 222 needing a fix the generic extractor can't make site-agnostically, add the file 223 back. Never keep a file whose only content is a restatement of the generic 224 base, and never annotate one as "nothing to add". 225 - Adding support for a new host is the most common change — the architecture 226 must keep it a single-file change: a host added to `supportedDomains`, plus — 227 only when the generic extractor gets that site wrong — one self-contained new 228 `extension/event-extractors/custom/.js` and a regenerated load list, 229 touching nothing else and assuming nothing about other extractors. 230 231 ## Capture policy — lessons land in the local packs 232 233 **The gcec local pack is this repo's capture surface.** Route each lesson to its 234 section here: extractor-automation to the "Extractor pipeline" section, 235 everything else to the fitting section. Mechanism before prose, per the canon's 236 local promotion ladder — `test-offline-list-sync` is this pack's worked example. 237 238 **Three kinds never land here, however strong the evidence** — filter on what a 239 lesson is *about* before picking a mechanism: 240 241 - **The owner's personal preferences** (which word means "merge it", tone, 242 summary style). They belong to the owner, are injected per-session, and change 243 without this repo hearing about it. 244 - **Claudinite loading mechanics** (which packs are declared, why a skill didn't 245 mount, why an injection missed). Engine plumbing, not project knowledge — a 246 real defect there goes upstream instead. 247 - **Anything derived from product requirements.** Packs carry 248 **development-process** lessons only; what the extension should do is 249 `dev/requirements/`'s territory, and restating it here will drift. 250 251 None of the three is mechanically checkable, so all three stay prose. 252

1	// gcec local check: `npm test` runs everything. Its `test` script is a single
2	// `node --test` invocation over a hand-kept list of glob patterns — one per test
3	// directory — so every committed *.test.{js,mjs,cjs} in the repo must be reached
4	// by one of them. The rule this converts is RULES.md's first testing invariant
5	// ("`npm test` runs everything ... `test:e2e` (heavy, CI-only)").
6	//
7	// Why a check and not just prose: the failure is silent in exactly the way a
8	// static scan is for. A test file in a directory no pattern reaches is simply
9	// never run — `node --test` doesn't error on a glob that matches nothing, npm
10	// exits 0, CI stays green, and the coverage is just gone with nothing red to say
11	// so. The pattern list has grown one entry at a time (extension-test/,
12	// dev/build/test/, dev/build/release/, four separate dev/requirements/ subtrees,
13	// the local pack's tasks, the pack's own .mjs fixtures); the next new test
14	// directory is one forgotten glob away from that silence.
15	//
16	// The one carve-out is READ FROM package.json, never hardcoded: the heavy,
17	// CI-only e2e suite is deliberately outside `npm test`, and it declares itself
18	// in `scripts["test:e2e"]`. A file matched by that script's patterns is covered
19	// by design, so the carve-out follows the e2e suite around instead of pinning a
20	// path here.
21	//
22	// ONE DIRECTION ONLY, on purpose (the same choice as
23	// extension-test/integration/supported-domains.test.js): a *stale* pattern — one
24	// matching nothing — is not asserted, because a literal path that no longer
25	// exists makes `node --test` fail loudly on the next run. Only the silent
26	// direction needs a guard.
27	//
28	// Local-pack check modules are dependency-free on purpose (see
29	// test-offline-list-sync.mjs's header): plain finding objects, no engine imports,
30	// so they also load under the repo's own `npm test` (pack.test.mjs). The engine
31	// already drops the vendored `.claudinite/shared/` canon from ctx.files, so the
32	// canon's own tests are structurally out of scope and need no exemption here.
33	const id = 'npm-test-glob-coverage';
34	const severity = 'blocking';
35	const doc = '.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/RULES.md';
36	const why =
37	  'node --test never errors on a glob that matches nothing — a test file no pattern ' +
38	  'reaches silently never runs, and npm test still exits 0';
39	
40	const isTestFile = (p) => /\.test\.(js|mjs|cjs)$/.test(p);
41	
42	// The file/glob arguments of a `node --test …` script line. Quotes come off (the
43	// globs are quoted so the shell can't expand them first); the binary and every
44	// flag drop out. A leftover non-pattern token can only ever fail to match, which
45	// under-reports rather than false-alarms.
46	function runnerPatterns(script) {
47	  if (typeof script !== 'string') return [];
48	  if (!/(^|\s)--test(\s|$)/.test(script)) return []; // not a glob-driven runner
49	  return script
50	    .split(/\s+/)
51	    .map((t) => t.replace(/^['"]/, '').replace(/['"]$/, ''))
52	    .filter((t) => t && t !== 'node' && !t.startsWith('-'));
53	}
54	
55	const ESCAPE_RE = /[.+^${}()|[\]\\]/g;
56	const STAR_STAR = '\u0000'; // placeholder for a whole `**` path segment
57	
58	// A minimal glob → matcher for those patterns, applied per path segment so `**`
59	// is only special as a segment of its own: `**` spans directories, `*` and `?`
60	// stay inside one segment. A pattern carrying no wildcard and no file extension
61	// is a DIRECTORY argument — `node --test <dir>` recurses — so it covers
62	// everything beneath it.
63	function toMatcher(pattern) {
64	  const p = pattern.replace(/\/+$/, '');
65	  if (!/[*?]/.test(p) && !/\.[a-z0-9]+$/i.test(p)) {
66	    return (f) => f === p || f.startsWith(`${p}/`);
67	  }
68	  const source = p
69	    .split('/')
70	    .map((seg) =>
71	      seg === '**'
72	        ? STAR_STAR
73	        : seg.replace(ESCAPE_RE, '\\$&').replace(/\*/g, '[^/]*').replace(/\?/g, '[^/]'),
74	    )
75	    .join('/')
76	    // A leading `**/` matches ZERO or more directories — that's what makes
77	    // extension-test/**/*.test.js cover extension-test/host-policy.test.js too.
78	    .split(`${STAR_STAR}/`)
79	    .join('(?:.*/)?')
80	    .split(`/${STAR_STAR}`)
81	    .join('(?:/.*)?')
82	    .split(STAR_STAR)
83	    .join('.*');
84	  const re = new RegExp(`^${source}$`);
85	  return (f) => re.test(f);
86	}
87	
88	const matchers = (patterns) => patterns.map(toMatcher);
89	const anyMatch = (ms, file) => ms.some((m) => m(file));
90	
91	export default {
92	  id,
93	  severity,
94	  description: "package.json's test script globs reach every committed test file",
95	  doc,
96	  why,
97	
98	  run(ctx) {
99	    const raw = ctx.read('package.json');
100	    if (!raw) return [];
101	    let scripts;
102	    try {
103	      scripts = JSON.parse(raw).scripts || {};
104	    } catch {
105	      return []; // malformed package.json breaks npm first — not this check's finding
106	    }
107	
108	    const covered = matchers(runnerPatterns(scripts.test));
109	    if (!covered.length) return []; // no glob-driven `test` script — nothing to enforce
110	    const exempt = matchers(runnerPatterns(scripts['test:e2e']));
111	
112	    // ctx.files is the whole repo under the engine's default `all` sweep; a
113	    // --changed run narrows it, which only ever under-reports.
114	    return ctx.files
115	      .filter(isTestFile)
116	      .filter((f) => !anyMatch(covered, f) && !anyMatch(exempt, f))
117	      .map((file) => ({
118	        rule: id,
119	        severity,
120	        file,
121	        line: null,
122	        what: `${file} is reached by no pattern in package.json's \`test\` script`,
123	        why,
124	        fix:
125	          'add a glob covering it to the `test` script in package.json — or, if it is a heavy ' +
126	          'CI-only test, to `test:e2e` (which this check reads as the declared carve-out)',
127	        doc,
128	      }));
129	  },
130	};

1	---
2	name: testing-guide
3	description: Map of this repo's test suites, the requirements model, and where each harness documents itself. Use before writing or changing tests here, adding a requirement case, or debugging a suite — the invariants live in the gcec pack's RULES.md; this is the deeper how-to.
4	---
5	
6	# Testing in this repo
7	
8	```sh
9	npm install
10	npm run test:live      # integration: the REVIEWED assertions for each supported site
11	npm run test:offline   # unit: internal tests of the extraction logic
12	npm run test:ui        # UI: rendered popup/icon vs. the stored snapshot image
13	npm run refresh:ui     # regenerate snapshots after an intentional UI change
14	npm run test:e2e       # heavy: real Chrome, CI-only (skips without CHROME_PATH)
15	npm test               # everything above except e2e
16	```
17	
18	The invariants (mirror tree, reviewed-contract cases, `REFERENCE_NOW` floor) are
19	always-loaded in the gcec pack's RULES.md. General test discipline (see-it-fail,
20	refusal-test mutation, green-twice, high-watermark gating) is canon.
21	Adding a cached live case is covered under "Live integration tests" below; the
22	generic-coverage gate's invariants are in the gcec pack's RULES.md.
23	
24	## The requirements model — every leaf has exactly one case
25	
26	The spec (`dev/requirements/requirements.md`) is numbered prose; it does NOT
27	tag how a leaf is verified. Each leaf has exactly one
28	`<kind>/cases/<slug>.<id>.case.js` — the **filename** names the leaf, the
29	**folder** names the kind (the single classifier; no `kind` field, no side
30	manifest — issues #429/#435). `dev/requirements/shared/kinds.js` auto-discovers
31	kinds; adding one is a self-contained folder drop (`<kind>/kind.js`). The
32	kinds: **popup** (image, the popup's real `render()`), **icon** (image, the
33	real `toolbar-icon.js` in a fake browser), **behavior** (a click/navigation —
34	no image; verified by `dev/requirements/behavior/events-view-actions.test.js`),
35	**extractor** (per supported host, real extractor against a real cached page),
36	**logic** (product rules, executable `verify()`), plus `tbd: true` for a leaf
37	not yet faithfully verified. `dev/requirements/requirements-coverage.test.js`
38	fails unless every leaf has exactly one case (and rejects a typo'd/duplicate
39	case, an unknown kind, or a non-image case smuggling in a PNG). Full model +
40	how-to-add-one: `dev/requirements/README.md`.
41	
42	⚠️ The behavior test **stubs** `chrome.tabs.create`/`window.close` — every leaf
43	is *claimed*, not every leaf *faithfully* verified (#435; the banner in
44	`requirements.md` says the same).
45	
46	## Live integration tests
47	
48	`dev/requirements/extractor/live.test.js` is driven by declarative JSON in
49	`expected/`: `expected.events` is the **complete, exact** array the extractor
50	produces — deep-equal on `title`/`start`/`end`/`location`/`ctz`/`details`, no
51	matchers, array length included. The page URL lives **only** in
52	`data/server-fetched/<name>.url` (single source of truth — the recorder and the
53	test both read it; never in the case file). Tests run offline against the
54	committed cached HTML, loaded into a DOM at the `.url`'s URL so hostname
55	detection behaves exactly as in Chrome. `test.yml` never fetches.
56	
57	**Adding one.** Usually you don't: file an `extractor-request` issue with the
58	event URL and the `create-extractor` task records the page, writes the
59	extractor, and opens the PR. To add a case by hand, land the `.url` alone first
60	— a committed `.url` with no sibling `.html` *is* the request the `create-extractor`
61	task sweeps for, so it fetches the page (ScraperAPI; this sandbox is bot-blocked)
62	and opens a PR carrying it. Merge that, then run `npm run test:live` and paste
63	the printed values into `expected/<name>.json` — never hand-write them.
64	
65	**Gardening.** When an event page is taken down, point `<name>.url` at a newer
66	event **and delete the stale `<name>.html`** in the same commit; that is the
67	whole re-record request. Until an HTML file exists, `test:live` fails with
68	`Missing cached HTML for "<name>"`, so land the refresh before (or with) the
69	case's updated `expected`.
70	
71	## UI snapshots
72	
73	`dev/requirements/shared/render/visual-snapshots.test.js` renders each case and
74	pixel-compares (pixelmatch, `MAX_DIFF_RATIO = 0`) against the committed PNG.
75	`render-snapshot.js` picks the renderer by the case's folder: `popup/` → the
76	shipped `render()` path; `icon/` → the real `toolbar-icon.js` under
77	`fake-chrome.js`. Rasterizing is satori + resvg — **not a screenshot**: a
78	constrained flexbox subset that buys determinism with no browser; the renderer
79	folds the real `popup.css` onto the DOM as inline styles (one styling source of
80	truth). Snapshots are authored in **en-US** (a guard test enforces it). After
81	an intentional popup/view/CSS/icon change: `npm run refresh:ui`, commit the
82	PNGs + inline gallery. On mismatch the test writes `.actual.png`/`.diff.png`
83	under `dev/requirements/shared/.artifacts/` (gitignored) — and a moved baseline
84	goes through the snapshot-approval skill, never silent regeneration.
85	
86	## Where each harness documents itself
87	
88	The *why* of every non-obvious harness decision lives in that file's own
89	header/inline comments (the file-local-footgun rule) — read the file when you
90	touch it; this is just the map:
91	
92	- Generic-coverage gate — `dev/requirements/extractor/generic-coverage/generic-coverage.js`
93	  (field-by-field comparison) + `generic-coverage.test.js` (the high-watermark
94	  gate, #240).
95	- UI snapshot renderer limits (satori/resvg, CSS inlining, tall-list clamp,
96	  `skipRender`) — `dev/requirements/shared/render/popup-renderer.js`; the
97	  pixel-exact diff + en-US guard — `visual-snapshots.test.js`; gestures —
98	  `actions.js`.
99	- Behavior verification (stubbed boundary, self-asserting coverage) —
100	  `dev/requirements/behavior/events-view-actions.test.js`.
101	- Two-column gallery generator (managed `<!-- req-gallery:<id> -->` lines only;
102	  the file is part-authored, NOT on the `ours` driver) —
103	  `dev/requirements/shared/build-requirements-gallery.js`, gated by
104	  `dev/requirements/shared/requirements-gallery.test.js`.
105	- "Does the extension load?" — two layers:
106	  `extension-test/integration/extension-loads.test.js` (always-on, Chrome-faithful
107	  `importScripts`, #146) and `dev/requirements/heavy/extension-load.chrome.test.js`
108	  (real Chrome, verify via CI).
109	- Requirement numbering is parsed by `dev/requirements/shared/ui-requirements.js`
110	  (numbers only — it does NOT classify leaves).
